**Title:** Edit-tool read-state expires after intervening Write within same session

**Statement:** When the Edit tool fails with "File has not been read yet" on a file the agent demonstrably touched earlier in the session, the cause is an intervening Write call. Write does NOT register as Read-state for the file. After a Write (or Write-without-prior-Read), Read must be called again before any subsequent Edit on that file.

**Operational rule:** Always Read before Edit if there was an intervening Write earlier in the session, OR if this is the first Edit on a file written in this session.

**Why it matters:** The failure mode is silent on multi-Edit batches — if two Edits target the same file in one message and the second's old_string was already partially edited by the first, the second silently fails with the same error AND the partial-state is the persisted state. Workflow consequence: agent claims "shipped two edits" when only one landed. Caught at S26 15:55 by user feedback; caught at S36 16:00 by error message in this very session.

**Title candidate:** Inverted-trigger primitives are an antipattern when substrate connectivity is poll-based

**Statement:** When designing a wake / notification mechanism against a substrate, first determine the substrate's connectivity model. If substrate is **outbound-only-poll** (consumer dials in, producer never dials consumer), there is no "push to consumer X" primitive. The correct wake mechanism is **state-write-as-wake**: the producer writes durable state that the consumer picks up on its next poll cycle. Designing an "inverted-trigger primitive" (call something that triggers a push to consumer) against poll-based substrate is structurally impossible — no such primitive exists, no SDK call can synthesize one, and design content that assumes such a primitive will fail at integration time.

**Why it matters:** the failure mode at integration is **silent for the producer side and infinite-timeout for the consumer side**. Producer's "trigger" call either no-ops or fails with a misleading error (e.g., "session created" instead of "session running"); consumer never wakes because no work was queued. By the time someone notices, the design assumption is propagated through multiple documents and decisions.

**Substrate-shapes this applies to (cross-reference for Cal):**
- **Anthropic Managed Agents:** outbound-only worker long-poll; wake-trigger is `sessions.create()` (state-write), not "push to recipient" — confirmed source: `claude-api` skill / `shared/managed-agents-self-hosted-sandboxes.md`.
- **Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY:** NOTIFY only wakes already-connected listeners; new listeners don't retroactively see past NOTIFYs. State-write to a queue table + LISTEN-driven consumer is the durable pattern.
- **Cloudflare Durable Objects:** alarm()-based wake; no inbound RPC primitive for DO-to-DO wake. State-write + alarm-set is the wake pattern.
- **Filesystem-watch substrates** (inotify, fsnotify): consumer dials in to watch; producer can only write files, not "notify" specific consumers.

The cross-substrate generalization is what makes this gotcha-class rather than specific-to-Anthropic.

**Operational rule:** for any wake/notification design, first answer "is substrate push-based or poll-based?" If poll-based: design state-write-as-wake. If push-based: SDK primitive exists. **Do not design inverted-trigger primitives against poll-based substrate.**
